bibliographic.title: The Role Of Audit Committees In Strengthening Governance And Risk Management In Banks: Evidence From Nepal
bibliographic.authors: Rajan Bikram Thapa, Alok Kumar, Surender Kumar Gupta, Ram Chandra Bhandari
bibliographic.citation_apa: Thapa, R. B., Kumar, A., Gupta, S. K., & Bhandari, R. C. (2025). The role of audit committees in strengthening governance and risk management in banks: Evidence from Nepal. International Journal of Environmental Sciences, 11(7s), 960–961.

methodology.method_family: quantitative secondary data analysis with confirmatory factor analysis and multiple regression
methodology.study_design: cross-sectional empirical study using secondary data from bank annual reports and central bank directives
methodology.sample_description: Nepalese banks; data drawn from annual reports and directives issued by Nepal Rastra Bank
methodology.technology_context: corporate governance audit committees in banking institutions; no LLM, generative AI, or conversational systems

eligibility.exclusion_reason: The study examines corporate governance and risk management via banking audit committees using secondary financial/regulatory data; it does not address LLMs, generative AI, conversational systems, chatbots, agents, RAG, or conversational governance.
eligibility.decision_rationale: Although the article scores on generic governance, banking, compliance, audit, and risk terms, the review scope requires governance of LLM-based conversational systems in regulated settings. The provided text contains zero references to LLMs, generative AI, conversational interfaces, or AI system oversight mechanisms. Governance here refers to board-level audit committee oversight of financial reporting and institutional risk, not AI or conversational governance.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Exclusion is unambiguous from title, abstract, and introduction: topic is audit committees in Nepalese banking with no AI or conversational technology content.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal based only on page 1 abstract and introduction. Methods (CFA, multiple regression) are stated but full sampling frame, model specification, results, and limitations are not present in the excerpt. Ethics not discussed in provided text.

cerqual.explanation: Within-scope relevance for conversational LLM governance is absent. Methodological detail in the excerpt is partial; only abstract-level claims about positive relationships are available without full results or limitations.

coding.theme: Corporate governance and risk management through audit committees in banking
coding.subtheme: Board-level audit oversight in Nepalese banks

synthesis.main_claim: Audit committees positively influence governance and risk management practices in Nepalese banks, with proactive risk assessment by the committee contributing to effective risk governance.
synthesis.contribution: Adds empirical evidence on audit committee effectiveness in South Asian banking using CFA and regression on secondary regulatory and annual report data.
synthesis.use_in_review: Exclude from central and supporting evidence pools. May serve only as distant contextual background on generic governance/audit/compliance in regulated banking if a separate non-AI governance boundary discussion is needed, but it does not inform conversational LLM governance.
